answer: The crystal multiplier is published, charged in harbor, and dawn lists each payment. A burst of registrations thus prices itself out, since the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The admission burn is multiplied by 2 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 4044 identities would post 1074 proofs and burn roughly 11 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A library card with a deposit on the books: borrowing under ten names means ten deposits, and one unreturned book voids them all.
